docs.description: The menu, as JSON: ["Rename", "-", {"value":"delete","label":"Delete","danger":true}]. An item is {value, label?, description?, icon?, href?, disabled?, danger?} (icon is text, such as an emoji: rich icons and content are the markup form's), {"divider":true} ("-" works too), a group heading {"group":"Move to"} (the items after it, up to the next heading or divider, are its group), or a submenu {label, children:[...]} nested up to 5 levels deep. An item with href is a link the browser follows (no sb-select). Server data: a new array replaces the whole tree, open or not.
Text of the default trigger, and the accessible name of trigger and menu.
Shown in a menu or submenu that has no items.
Preferred side and alignment of the menu; it flips and shifts when there is no room. Submenus always open to the inline end and flip to the start.

radio makes the root menu one radio group, for a menu that shows a current choice; a group inside a submenu is type:"radio" on that item instead. The group reaches into its submenus, and a dropdown holds one group.

Radio group: the checked value, owned by the server — for a choice in a submenu the item values from the group root down, joined with dots ("date.newest"). A new value from the server wins (value="" clears it); the live value is the value property.
Radio group: :state(pending) on the host and on the chosen item while the local value differs from the server's value attribute (see revert()).

Revision of the server's value, for commands: the server bumps it with every command it answers for this field, applied or refused. A new rev makes the value attribute win even when it is unchanged, so a refused edit reverts.
The page's word that a command is on its way (e.g. data-attr:pending="$_saving"): :state(pending) and aria-busy while present. It adds to confirm's pending, never clears it.

Open when present. The server adding or removing the attribute opens or closes the menu; re-sent identical markup leaves the local state alone. Never reflected: use the open property, show() and hide() from the client.
Disable the trigger (and close the menu).
Name reported in sb-select and sb-change (e.g. the field of a command).

slots.name: trigger
slots.description: Content of the trigger button (text, an icon). The component provides the button itself, with all the ARIA on it.

slots.name: item
slots.description:
Menu items as markup instead of items: , Label for a link, or
for a divider.
Move to
is a group heading: the items after it, up to the next heading or divider, are its group (text only). A submenu is data-children='[…]' (the same JSON as items). They are read as data; items wins when it is not empty. Rich items: an element marked data-icon inside the item (an inline ) is copied into the row's icon place, and other elements in it (a lozenge) are copied into the row in place of the text, which stays the row's accessible name; a radio trigger shows the chosen item the same way. Copies keep their attributes, so part="…" and an inline style reach them from the page.

events.name: sb-select
events.description: A plain item was chosen; the whole menu closes. detail: { name, value }: ready for a command. A submenu parent never reports a value, an item of a radio group reports sb-change instead, and a link reports nothing: the browser follows it.

events.name: sb-change
events.description: Radio group: an item of the group was chosen. detail: { name, value }, the value being the dotted path for a choice inside a submenu: ready for a command.

events.name: sb-open
events.description: The menu opened (the root; submenus are view state and stay quiet).

events.name: sb-close
events.description: The menu closed. detail: { reason }: item, escape, outside, scroll, tab, trigger, server or api.
